productionIssuerDependencyGraph.action: Bind accepted canonical binaries, actual host/member identities, addresses/ports and HA source evidence to a new cluster deployment contract; no loopback fixture identity is accepted.
After separate exact GO, verify each proposed new root and role/policy name absent; create only the owned registration roots and retain complete independent readbacks. Any existing entry stops.

Under a separately reviewed secure issuer, generate one new independent CA and per-member leaf key/certificate; SANs must equal the actually bound addresses/names. Private keys remain private; public chains/full hashes and issuer receipts are required.

Initialize the new cluster once, retain actual clusterId/member evidence and private recovery custody, and read back the real native profile. Never import fixture root tokens, unseal keys, role IDs or SecretIDs.

Render exact per-host ACL from the installed AuthBus operation closure and real profile/grant mapping: canonical read grants separated from per-host inbox proposals; freeze policy hash, create once and independently read back.

Create each new per-host AppRole once with explicitly reviewed token/SecretID TTL and use limits; obtain RoleID and issue SecretID from real authenticated responses. Bind response, issuer/cluster, policy hash and the private generation files without public values.

Use actual issued tokens for lookup-self before renewal, renewal and lookup-self after renewal, unassigned rejection, revoke and revoked rejection. HTTP200 alone is not TTL/expiry extension evidence. Unknown stops without replay.

For one host at a time, obtain an exact private rollback capsule and real service writer custody, then change only four client connection fields under expected-before/after guards. Keep models, enabled, provider, refresh/quota, order, caches and hold directives unchanged.
Qualify actual persistence/cold-start and one strict inverse for that host under separate manager GO. Existing inactive or held services are not automatically started or released.

Register the newly introduced cluster/credential backup dependency explicitly, prove one source-bound encrypted capture/restore on the accepted product, and only then consider separately authorized legacy cleanup.
